Senator Bailey, Representative Mathiesen, and members of the Health
Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee, I am Bob Carey,
Superintendent of Insurance. I am here today to testify in support of LD 131.

By way of background, as an alternative to obtaining commercial workers'

compensation insurance, an employer can form a joint and several alternative

known as a self-insured group ("SIG"). The majority of Maine SIGs have

provided stable lovver-oostWorl<e1"s' compensation insurance since the early 1990s.

While SIGs provide a stable lower-cost alternative to commercial workers'

compensation insurance, SIG coverage is limited to employees working in the state

of Maine. Maine employers with employees Working in other' states~ could not -

cover these workers under the SIG.

Last session, the Legislature enacted L.D. 1372, which authorized the
formation of group self-insured reinsurance fronting arrangements. Fronting
companies formed pursuant to this law were to be owned by one or more SIGs or by a group self-insured reinsurance account, and were intended to address out-ofstate workers' compensation coverage issues faced by Maine employers.
As directed by the Legislature, the Bureau of Insurance developed and provisionally adopted Rule Chapter 255 to implement the fronting company legislation. The provisions of this rule proved to be unacceptable to the committee
Accordingly, the Bureau returned to the drawing board and reopened discussions
with the proponents of the original bill. In doing so, we sought to find a solution
that protected both workers and employers, first and foremost, as Well as respected the authority of each state to set parameters for its workers' compensation system.
The outcome of these discussions was a solution that worked for everyone. The SIGs behind L.D. 1372 chose to form a` workers' compensation insurance company under the laws of Delaware. The Delaware insurance company will address SIG members' out-of-state workers' compensation coverage issues.
With no further interest in forming a fronting company and with no interest expressed by any other company, the Bureau supports this bill to repeal these statutes and with it our obligation to do major substantive rulemaking on this issue.
Thank you. I would be glad to answer any questions now or at the work
session.
